# ntfy-flyio

Self-hosted [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) on Fly.io: generic push-notification
server config, usable from any client of the ntfy HTTP API (curl, scripts,
CI, other apps).

Configured with a 30-day scheduled-delivery window rather than ntfy.sh's
default 3-day cap, which happens to suit long-lead reminders well.

My own use case for this instance is feeding the Obsidian
[Reminder](https://github.com/uphy/obsidian-reminder) plugin so Android
gets a real system notification for vault tasks even when Obsidian itself
is closed — see `SETUP-RUNBOOK.md` for that specific setup. That part is
entirely optional; the server itself doesn't care what publishes to it.

## Why self-hosted

- Task text never transits ntfy.sh.
- `message-delay-limit` raised to 30 days (public ntfy.sh caps scheduled
  delivery at 3 days).
- Single private topic, token-authenticated, `deny-all` default access.

## Important: this app must stay always-on

Unlike the other `*-flyio` repos in this account, **auto-stop is disabled**
(`auto_stop_machines = false`, `min_machines_running = 1`). ntfy delivers
scheduled messages from an in-process timer — a stopped machine cannot wake
itself to deliver a due reminder. Do not copy the auto-stop pattern from
`obsidian-livesync-flyio` into this app.

## Layout

- `fly.toml` — app config: 1 shared CPU, 256MB, 1GB volume at
  `/var/lib/ntfy` for the message cache and auth DB.
- `server.yml` — ntfy server config, injected into the image via
  `[[files]]` and mounted at `/etc/ntfy/server.yml`.

## Setup

See `SETUP-RUNBOOK.md` for first deploy and user/token creation (generic —
applies to any ntfy use case). Steps 5-7 in that file are specific to the
Obsidian reminders use case; skip them if that's not your goal.

## Cost

shared-cpu-1x 256MB always-on + 1GB volume: roughly $2-3/mo.
